- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 3–5% buffer to forecast lows.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots the next period; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–5%.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force a mean-reversion correction toward prior 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 14-day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish → bearish” transitions, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast magnitude by 3–7% in subsequent periods.
